task1.title: Renewable energy supply
task1.prompt: The bar chart below shows the proportion of renewable energy of total supply in 2000, 2004, and 2007.

chartDesc.title: renewable energy of the total supply
chartDesc.overview: Norway and Iceland supplied a significantly higher proportion of renewable energy compared to Australia and Germany across all three years. Norway showed the largest overall increase, while Australia consistently had the lowest share.
unreadable: Exact numerical value labels above the bars are omitted; figures are read against the y-axis grid lines.
keyFeatures: Norway had the highest share of renewable energy, rising from approximately 62% in 2000 to nearly 78% in 2007.
Australia recorded the lowest proportion, remaining at or below 10% throughout (8% in 2000, 10% in 2004, and 9% in 2007).
Germany experienced steady growth from 12% in 2000 to 17% in 2007.
Iceland peaked at around 59% in 2004 before decreasing slightly to 55% in 2007.

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparison where relevant.
task1.sampleBand5:
The bar chart shows the proportion of renewable energy used in total energy supply for three years: 2000, 2004, and 2007.

In 2000, the amount of renewable energy was 6%. Then, in the year of 2004, it went up to 7%. After this, in 2007, it increased again to 9%. So, it went up every time.

It is clear that renewable energy use was increasing. More and more people used it over the years. The biggest change was between 2004 and 2007.

Overall, the bar chart shows a positive trend for renewable energy. It was always going up, even though the numbers are not very big.
task1.sampleBand6:
The bar chart shows the proportion of renewable energy as a percentage of the total energy supply in a number of years, specifically 2000, 2004 and 2007.

Overall, it is clear that the proportion of renewable energy fluctuated over the period given. There were some increases and decreases, but the general trend was an upward one. It is also noticeable that the proportion was always below a quarter of the total energy supply.

In 2000, the proportion of renewable energy was around 17%. This fell slightly to just under 16% in 2004. However, by 2007, this had risen to approximately 22%. So, although there was a decrease initially, the proportion ended at a higher level than it started. The biggest increase was between 2004 and 2007. It can be seen that the renewable energy made up a small part of the total energy.
task1.sampleBand7:
The bar chart illustrates the proportion of renewable energy sources as a percentage of total energy supply across a number of countries in the years 2000, 2004, and 2007.

Overall, it is clear that the proportion of renewable energy experienced fluctuations across the three specified years. While some countries saw an increase in their renewable energy usage, others showed a decrease. It is also readily apparent that Iceland consistently had the highest proportion of renewable energy in its total supply.

In 2000, Iceland stood out significantly with approximately 70% of its energy coming from renewable sources. This figure remained relatively stable, with only a slight increase to around 72% by 2007. Sweden, on the other hand, started at around 48% in 2000, witnessing a gradual decline to approximately 45% in 2004 before slightly recovering to around 52% in 2007.

Other countries showed different patterns. While Italy's renewable energy proportion remained relatively consistent at around 5% throughout the period, the proportion in Canada showed an upward trend, rising from approximately 22% in 2000 to around 26% in 2007. The United States had the lowest percentage overall, starting at about 3% and reaching only around 6% by 2007.
task1.sampleBand8:
The bar chart illustrates the proportion of total energy derived from renewable sources in a given nation across the years 2000, 2004, and 2007.

Overall, it is immediately apparent that the percentage of renewable energy witnessed an increase over the period. Furthermore, the most significant growth occurred between 2004 and 2007. While there were fluctuations, the overall trend indicates a gradual shift towards greater reliance on renewable energy sources.

In 2000, the proportion of renewable energy stood at approximately 5%. This figure remained relatively stable until 2004, experiencing only a marginal increase. However, between 2004 and 2007, there was a noticeable surge, with the percentage climbing to around 8%. This represents a significant increase compared to the earlier period. While not explicitly stated, this increase may be attributable to a concerted effort to promote and invest in renewable energy technologies during this time.

In conclusion, the data suggests a positive trend in the adoption of renewable energy sources. Although the initial growth was slow, the accelerated pace of increase between 2004 and 2007 suggests a promising future for renewable energy adoption.
task1.sampleBand9:
The bar chart elucidates the proportion of total energy derived from renewable sources across a selection of countries in the years 2000, 2004, and 2007.

Overall, it is immediately apparent that the contribution of renewable energy to total supply witnessed an upward trend across all nations during the observed period. Furthermore, the proportion of renewable energy was consistently highest in Iceland and lowest in the United Kingdom.

In 2000, Iceland led the way with approximately 30% of its energy sourced from renewable means, followed by Sweden at around 17%. Italy and the UK lagged considerably behind, with approximately 2% and 1% respectively. By 2004, all countries had experienced an increase in renewable energy usage. Iceland’s proportion had risen substantially to almost 45%, while Sweden’s reached close to 20%. Italy doubled its proportion to 4%, and the UK experienced a modest increase to 2%.

The trend of increased renewable energy usage continued into 2007. Iceland maintained its position as the leader, with approximately 53% of its total energy coming from renewable sources. Sweden also saw further growth, reaching around 22%. Italy nearly doubled again to 7%, while the UK, although still the lowest, showed a more marked increase to around 5%. In summary, although the UK's growth seems small, it is important to note that it still represents a substantial increase percentage-wise, despite remaining at the bottom of the comparison.
task1.sampleAnswer:
The bar chart compares the percentage of renewable energy in the total energy supply across several countries in three different years: 2000, 2004, and 2007. Overall, while most countries showed increases in renewable energy usage, the proportions varied significantly between nations.

In 2000, Iceland had by far the highest proportion of renewable energy at approximately 70% of its total supply, followed by Norway at around 45%. New Zealand and Sweden both had figures of approximately 30%, while other countries such as the USA, UK, and Japan had much lower proportions, all below 10%.

By 2007, most countries had increased their renewable energy usage. Iceland remained the leader, increasing slightly to about 75%. Norway also showed growth, reaching approximately 55%. Sweden demonstrated notable improvement, rising to about 40%. New Zealand maintained its position at around 30%.

Interestingly, some countries showed minimal change over the period. The USA, UK, Germany, and Japan all remained below 15% throughout the seven-year period, although each showed slight increases. The data suggests that countries with already high renewable energy usage continued to lead, while those starting from low bases made only modest progress.

Ustunli diagrammada qayta tiklanadigan energiya manbalarining umumiy energiya ta'minotidagi foiz nisbati bir qator yillar, xususan, 2000, 2004 va 2007 yillarda ko'rsatilgan.

Ustunli diagramma bir qator mamlakatlar bo'ylab 2000, 2004 va 2007-yillarda qayta tiklanuvchi energiya manbalarining umumiy energiya ta'minotidagi foizini ko'rsatadi.

Shvetsiya esa, aksincha, 2000-yilda taxminan 48 foizdan boshlangan bo'lib, 2004-yilda taxminan 45 foizga asta-sekin pasayishga guvoh bo'ldi, so'ngra 2007-yilda biroz tiklanib, taxminan 52 foizni tashkil etdi.

Boshqa mamlakatlar turli xil naqshlarni ko'rsatdi. Italiyaning qayta tiklanuvchi energiya ulushi butun davr davomida taxminan 5 foizda nisbatan barqaror bo'lib qolgan bo'lsa, Kanadada bu ko'rsatkich yuqoriga qarab o'sish tendentsiyasini ko'rsatdi, 2000-yildagi taxminan 22 foizdan 2007-yilda taxminan 26 foizga ko'tarildi. Ochiq aytilmagan bo'lsa-da, bu o'sish shu vaqt ichida qayta tiklanadigan energiya texnologiyalarini targ'ib qilish va ularga sarmoya kiritish bo'yicha uyushgan harakat bilan bog'liq bo'lishi mumkin.

Xulosa qilib aytganda, ma'lumotlar qayta tiklanadigan energiya manbalarini qabul qilishda ijobiy tendentsiyani ko'rsatadi. Umuman olganda, shuni darhol anglash mumkinki, kuzatilgan davr mobaynida barcha davlatlarda umumiy ta'minotga qayta tiklanadigan energiyaning hissasi o'sib borish tendentsiyasiga ega bo'lgan. Islandiyaning ulushi sezilarli darajada oshib deyarli 45% ga yetdi, Shvetsiyaniki esa 20% ga yaqinlashdi. Italiya o'z ulushini ikki baravar oshirib 4% ga, Buyuk Britaniya esa kichik o'sishni boshdan kechirdi va 2% ga yetdi.

Qayta tiklanadigan energiyadan foydalanishning o'sish tendentsiyasi 2007-yilgacha davom etdi. Islandiya umumiy energiyasining taxminan 53 foizi qayta tiklanadigan manbalardan kelgan holda o'z mavqeini saqlab qoldi. Shvetsiya ham o'sishni ko'rsatdi va taxminan 22% ga yetdi. Italiya yana deyarli ikki baravar oshib 7% ga yetdi, Buyuk Britaniya esa, garchi hali ham eng past bo'lsa-da, taxminan 5% ga yanada sezilarli o'sishni ko'rsatdi. Xulosa qilib aytganda, Buyuk Britaniyaning o'sishi kichik bo'lib tuyulsa-da, shuni ta'kidlash kerakki, u taqqoslashning eng pastki qismida qolishiga qaramay, u hali ham foiz hisobida sezilarli o'sishni anglatadi.

task2.title: TV content and child behaviour
task2.prompt: Some people say that what children watch on TV influences their behaviour while others say the amount of time children spend watching TV influences their behaviour. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
task2.instruction: Discuss both views and give your opinion.
task2.sampleBand5:
Television is very common now, and children watch it a lot. Some people think the shows they watch make them behave in certain ways. Others think it's just the time they spend watching TV that changes them. I think both are important.

On the one hand, what children see on TV can be a big influence. If they watch violent cartoons, they might think its okay to hit their friends. Programs that show people being unkind can make children think that's how they should act too. Also, adverts can make children want things they don't need, and this can lead to arguments with their parents. So, the content is important.

However, the amount of time spent watching TV is also a problem. If children spend too long watching TV, they are not doing other things like playing outside or reading. This can affect their health and their brain development. They might not learn social skills because they are not interacting with other children. Also, they might not do their homework, which can affect their grades in school. It is like a waste of time.

In conclusion, both the content of TV programs and the amount of time children spend watching them can influence their behaviour. Parents should be careful about what their children watch and how long they watch it for. They should also encourage them to do other activities. It is important to have a balance.
task2.sampleBand6:
It is often debated whether the content of television programs or the amount of time children spend watching TV has a greater impact on their behaviour. Both views have merit, and it is important to consider both sides of the argument before forming an opinion. On the one hand, the content that children are exposed to can certainly influence them.

If children regularly watch violent programs, they may become desensitized to violence and more likely to engage in aggressive behaviour. Similarly, if they watch shows that promote unhealthy lifestyles, such as excessive consumption of junk food, it could have a negative impact on their own habits. Programs with positive role models, however, can encourage children to develop good values and behaviours. The influence of content is therefore undeniable, and parents should be mindful of what their children are watching.

However, the amount of time spent watching TV is also a significant factor. Even if the content is relatively harmless, spending too much time in front of the television can have detrimental effects. Children who spend hours watching TV are less likely to engage in physical activity, which can lead to obesity and other health problems. They may also have less time for other important activities, such as reading, playing, and socializing with friends and family. This can affect their cognitive and social development. It is also believed that too much screen time can affect their attention spans.

In conclusion, both the content and the amount of time spent watching TV can influence children's behaviour. While the content can shape their values and attitudes, the amount of time spent watching can affect their physical and cognitive development. In my opinion, both factors are important, and parents should strive to find a balance between allowing children to enjoy TV and ensuring they are not negatively affected by it.
task2.sampleBand7:
The question of how television impacts children's behaviour is a subject of considerable debate. While some argue that the content of programmes is the primary influence, others believe that the sheer amount of time spent watching TV is the more significant factor. Both perspectives have merit, and in my opinion, both contribute to shaping a child's behaviour, although the amount of time may be the more pervasive influence.

Those who emphasise the influence of content often point to the potential for exposure to violence, inappropriate language, or unrealistic portrayals of life. It is argued that children, especially those who are very young, are highly impressionable and may imitate what they see on screen. For instance, a child repeatedly exposed to aggressive behaviour in cartoons might display similar tendencies in their own interactions. Furthermore, the values and attitudes presented in television programmes can shape a child's understanding of the world and their place in it. However, this view overlooks the role of parents and educators in mediating these influences.

Conversely, the argument that the amount of time spent watching TV is more influential suggests that excessive viewing can displace other important activities. Children who spend hours in front of the television are less likely to engage in physical activity, read books, or interact with family and friends. This can lead to a range of negative consequences, including obesity, poor social skills, and reduced academic performance. Moreover, prolonged screen time can be detrimental to a child's cognitive development, as it may hinder the development of critical thinking and problem-solving skills. While the content may be harmless, the sheer volume of viewing can still have a significant impact.

In conclusion, while the content of television programmes undoubtedly plays a role in shaping children's behaviour, the amount of time spent watching TV is arguably a more significant factor. The displacement of essential activities and the potential for cognitive impairment associated with excessive viewing can have far-reaching consequences. Therefore, parents should strive to strike a balance, ensuring that children have access to age-appropriate and educational content while also limiting their overall screen time and encouraging other beneficial activities. It is not simply what children watch, but how much they watch that matters.
task2.sampleBand8:
The debate surrounding the influences on children's behaviour often centres on television, with some arguing that the content of programmes is the primary factor, while others believe that the sheer amount of time spent watching TV is more significant. Both perspectives hold a degree of validity, and this essay will explore these viewpoints before offering a considered opinion.

Proponents of the content argument suggest that what children watch directly shapes their understanding of the world and their behaviour. For example, exposure to violent cartoons or programmes that glamorise antisocial behaviour could desensitise children to violence or lead them to emulate negative role models. Educational programmes, conversely, can foster positive values and expand their knowledge base. There is ample research suggesting a correlation between media consumption and behaviour, though establishing a definitive causal link remains complex. Furthermore, the ubiquitous nature of advertising within children's programming can influence their desires and materialistic tendencies.

Conversely, the 'time spent' argument posits that regardless of the content, excessive television viewing can negatively impact a child's development. Spending countless hours glued to the screen reduces opportunities for crucial social interaction, physical activity, and creative play. This can lead to social isolation, obesity, and a stunted development of crucial cognitive and social skills. Even seemingly harmless programmes can contribute to this problem if they displace more beneficial activities. Children need diverse experiences to develop holistically, and excessive screen time inevitably limits these opportunities. This is especially true for very young children whose brains are rapidly developing, and for whom real-world experiences are paramount.

In conclusion, while the content of television programmes certainly plays a role in shaping children's behaviour, I believe that the amount of time spent watching TV is ultimately the more significant factor. Even positive content can be detrimental if it consumes too much of a child's time, crowding out other essential experiences. Therefore, parents should focus on establishing healthy boundaries around screen time, encouraging a balanced lifestyle that incorporates a variety of activities. Striking this balance is crucial for fostering well-rounded and healthy development. To mitigate the negative effects of prolonged viewing, families should actively engage in discussions about the programs watched, thereby providing context and critical analysis.
task2.sampleBand9:
The debate surrounding the impact of television on children's behaviour often centres on two key perspectives: the content they consume and the duration of their viewing. While both aspects undoubtedly play a role, their relative influence is a complex issue worthy of careful consideration. I believe that the content children watch is ultimately more influential, although the amount of time spent viewing certainly exacerbates any negative effects.

Proponents of the "content matters most" argument highlight the power of modelling. Children are highly impressionable and learn by observing the behaviours portrayed on screen. If they are consistently exposed to violence, aggression, or disrespectful attitudes, they are more likely to internalise and replicate these behaviours in their own interactions. Educational programmes, on the other hand, can foster positive values such as empathy, cooperation, and critical thinking. Furthermore, the narratives children engage with can shape their understanding of the world, influencing their beliefs, aspirations, and even their sense of identity. Therefore, controlling the type of programmes children access is crucial for promoting healthy development.

Conversely, the "time spent" argument posits that excessive television viewing, regardless of content, can negatively impact behaviour. Spending countless hours glued to the screen reduces opportunities for crucial real-world experiences, such as playing outdoors, engaging in social interactions, and pursuing hobbies. This can lead to social isolation, attention deficits, and a decline in physical health. Prolonged screen time has also been linked to sleep disturbances, which can further affect mood, concentration, and overall well-being. Therefore, limiting the amount of time children spend watching television is essential for preventing these negative consequences.

In my opinion, while excessive screen time is undoubtedly detrimental, the *type* of content children are exposed to has a more profound and lasting impact on their behaviour. A child who watches a moderate amount of educational and enriching programmes is likely to develop more positively than a child who spends the same amount of time watching violent or inappropriate content. However, it is important to acknowledge that the two factors are interconnected. The more time children spend watching television, the greater the potential for exposure to harmful content, and the more likely they are to be influenced by it. Ultimately, a balanced approach is required, one that prioritises both the quality and quantity of television viewing. Parents should actively monitor their children's viewing habits, selecting age-appropriate and educational programmes while also encouraging them to engage in a variety of other activities. This multifaceted strategy offers the best chance of mitigating the negative effects of television and harnessing its potential as a positive influence.

In conclusion, while both the content and duration of television viewing influence children's behaviour, the content appears to be the more significant factor. By carefully curating the programmes children watch and limiting their overall screen time, parents can help to ensure that television serves as a valuable tool for learning and development, rather than a source of negative influence. This proactive approach is paramount in navigating the complexities of modern childhood.
task2.sampleAnswer:
The impact of television on children's behavior has long been a subject of debate among parents, educators, and researchers. While some emphasize the importance of program content, others focus on the duration of viewing time. This essay will examine both perspectives before presenting my own view.

Those who believe that content is the primary factor argue that children are highly impressionable and tend to imitate what they see on screen. Violent programs may normalize aggressive behavior, while educational shows can promote positive social skills and cognitive development. From this perspective, carefully curated programming can be beneficial regardless of how long children watch. Research has shown that children who view prosocial content demonstrate more empathy and cooperative behavior than those exposed to violent media.

Conversely, proponents of the view that viewing time matters more contend that excessive television watching, regardless of content, has negative effects on children. Extended screen time reduces physical activity, contributing to obesity and related health problems. It also displaces time that could be spent on more beneficial activities such as reading, playing outdoors, or interacting with family and friends. Furthermore, prolonged television viewing has been linked to attention problems and reduced academic performance.

In my opinion, both factors are important, but I believe that content has a more significant influence on behavior. While limiting screen time is certainly advisable, the type of programs children watch has a more direct impact on the values and behaviors they develop. A child who watches two hours of educational programming is likely to benefit more than one who watches thirty minutes of violent content.

In conclusion, ideally, parents should monitor both what their children watch and for how long, but prioritizing appropriate content is more crucial for healthy behavioral development.

Televizor hozir juda keng tarqalgan va bolalar uni ko'p tomosha qilishadi. Ba'zi odamlar ularning tomosha qilayotgan ko'rsatuvlari ularni ma'lum tarzda o'zini tutishga majbur qiladi deb o'ylashadi. Boshqalar esa, bu faqat televizorni tomosha qilishga sarflaydigan vaqti ularni o'zgartiradi deb o'ylashadi. Men ikkalasi ham muhim deb o'ylayman.

Bir tomondan, bolalar televizorda ko'rgan narsalar katta ta'sir ko'rsatishi mumkin. Agar ular zo'ravon multfilmlarni tomosha qilsalar, ular do'stlarini urish yaxshi deb o'ylashlari mumkin. Odamlarning mehribon bo'lmaganini ko'rsatadigan dasturlar bolalarni xuddi shunday harakat qilishlari kerak deb o'ylashlariga olib kelishi mumkin. Shuningdek, reklamalar bolalarni ularga kerak bo'lmagan narsalarni xohlashga majbur qilishi mumkin va bu ota-onalari bilan janjallarga olib kelishi mumkin. Demak, kontent muhim.

Biroq, televizor tomosha qilishga sarflangan vaqt miqdori ham muammo. Agar bolalar televizorni tomosha qilishga juda ko'p vaqt sarflashsa, ular tashqarida o'ynash yoki o'qish kabi boshqa ishlarni qilmaydilar. Bu ularning sog'lig'iga va miya rivojlanishiga ta'sir qilishi mumkin. Ular boshqa bolalar bilan muloqot qilmasligi sababli ijtimoiy ko'nikmalarni o'rganmasligi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, ular uy vazifalarini qilmasliklari mumkin, bu esa maktabdagi baholariga ta'sir qilishi mumkin. Bu vaqtni behuda sarflashga o'xshaydi.

Xulosa qilib aytganda, televizor dasturlarining mazmuni ham, bolalarning ularni tomosha qilishga sarflagan vaqti ham ularning xulq-atvoriga ta'sir qilishi mumkin. Ota-onalar bolalarining nima tomosha qilayotganiga va qancha vaqt tomosha qilayotganiga e'tiborli bo'lishlari kerak. Ular, shuningdek, ularni boshqa faoliyatlar bilan shug'ullanishga undashlari kerak. Muvozanatni saqlash muhim.

Televideniye dasturlarining mazmuni yoki bolalarning televizor ko'rishga sarflaydigan vaqti ularning xulq-atvoriga qaysi biri ko'proq ta'sir qilishi ko'p bahs qilinadi. Ikkala nuqtai nazar ham o'rinli va fikr bildirishdan oldin argumentning ikkala tomonini ham ko'rib chiqish muhimdir. Bir tomondan, bolalar duch keladigan mazmun ularga albatta ta'sir qilishi mumkin.

Agar bolalar doimiy ravishda zo'ravonlik dasturlarini ko'rishsa, ular zo'ravonlikka nisbatan sezgirlikni yo'qotishi va tajovuzkor xatti-harakatlarda qatnashish ehtimoli ko'proq bo'lishi mumkin. Xuddi shunday, agar ular zararli turmush tarzini targ'ib qiluvchi ko'rsatuvlarni tomosha qilsalar, masalan, keraksiz ovqatlarni haddan tashqari iste'mol qilish, bu ularning o'z odatlariga salbiy ta'sir ko'rsatishi mumkin.
